text: Thornbury Press has acquired the publishing rights to The Glass Cartographer, according to a contract filed Monday with the fictive National Books Registry and confirmed by two people familiar with the deal. The novel, by Elian Drove, had been shopped to several houses after a seven-city auction last month. Thornbury’s agreement covers North American print, digital and audio editions, with first publication set for autumn 2027, said the registry filing. Financial terms were not disclosed, but one person briefed on the negotiations described the advance as “seven figures, comfortably.” The book, a historical mystery set in the port city of Valmere, has been widely touted by industry observers as one of the season’s most competitive acquisitions.
